headline: Sixteen And Oh Is Dead. Chris Scored The Fewest Points In The League.
kicker: (99.18, 0-13 in all-play. Tyler Shough 19.7 on the bench. Even the best lineup goes 0-2.)
lede: Chris was 16-0. Eight head-to-head wins, eight median wins, $95 of FAAB he never needed. In Week 9 he scored 99.18, the lowest score in the league, 0-13 in all-play. Josh Allen started for 13.86 with Tyler Shough's 19.7 on the bench. Tony Pollard was on bye. Tyler Higbee, picked up Wednesday morning, scored 1.8 at tight end. His best lineup scores 105.02 and still loses both games. Nathan beat him by 11.72 with Kirk Cousins on the bench again. Barrett scored 178.78, the highest score of the season, and takes first in the power rankings. Jon paid $20 for Adonai Mitchell, the league's most reliable zero, started him, and got the zero. Greg (Miley) benched Bryce Young for 21.34 and started Jared Goff for 6.30. Darrius finally benched Keenan Allen in the right week.

sections.awards: Fourteen citations. One undefeated season ended, one season high, and a $20 bid on a receiver whose whole reputation is zero.
sections.power: Season to date: record, points, all-play and this week's form, weighted, with movement from last week. Best lineup is the record each team would own if it had started its best legal lineup every week, everyone else exactly as they played. The tax is the difference: wins left on your own bench. Barrett is first for the first time all season, after seven straight weeks of Chris.
sections.median: Week 9's line was 114.04. Maclane cleared it by 0.88 with a perfect lineup. Jon missed it by 0.88 with a perfect lineup. Will and Maclane lost their games and got a win here; Nathan and Jon won theirs and lost here. Chris missed it by 14.86, his first loss to the median all season. Right of the line is a win.
sections.standings: Week 9 scoring, both results, and how much of your own roster you managed to start. Efficiency is what you scored over what your best legal lineup would have scored. Injured reserve does not count against you. Two teams hit 100.0 percent, Maclane and Jon, and they finished 0.88 either side of the median.
sections.bench: 147.58 points of lineup regret this week, down from 158.90. Greg (Miley) leads with 26.14, most of it a 21.34 quarterback on the bench.
sections.faab: Every dollar of Week 9, audited. $71 spent, 32 adds. The two biggest bids, $21 and $20, both started and scored 2.1 points between them.
sections.money: Auction dollars against everything each player has scored so far, started or not. Jordan Love: $2, 192.02 points. A.J. Brown: $45, 14.6.
sections.studs: The best and worst starts of Week 9, measured against what Yahoo thought they would do. Two quarterbacks who cost three dollars between them scored 72.54.
sections.games: The long version, closest game first.

newsletter.intro: Chris lost. Both games. To Nathan and to a number. Barrett scored the most points anyone has scored all year and now sits alone in first. Find your team below; everyone got one.

games.note: The closest game of the week, 1.34, and the first win in five for Jon. He played his second straight perfect lineup, and it was perfect for the same reason Abhishek's was last week: all five bench players scored zero. A.J. Brown, David Montgomery, Jaylen Warren, Dontayvion Wicks, Deshaun Watson, 0.00 each. On Wednesday Jon paid $20 for Adonai Mitchell, the receiver Greg (IR) started for 0.00 in Week 7 and this site called the league's most reliable zero. Jon started him at receiver. 0.00, on a 9.53 projection. Bijan Robinson ($69) finally showed up for 24.7 and the Packers scored 16.98. 113.16, the eighth score in the league for the second straight week: missed the median by 0.88 after missing it by 1.54. A.J. Brown: 14.6 points in nine weeks, $45. Nishil lost by 1.34 and missed the median by 2.22, 0-2. His best lineup was 127.42 and wins both. Jordan Watkins, a Wednesday pickup, scored 16.6 on the bench. Mack Hollins, added at 12:40 on Sunday, scored 11.1 on the bench. Caleb Douglas 10.0 on the bench. DJ Moore started at flex for 5.1. Drake Maye threw three touchdowns and three interceptions. 15.60 points of regret, 40 moves, 4-14.

Three straight head-to-head wins for Anuj, after 0-6. 125.88, 2-0, the second sweep in a row. Bucky Irving scored 26.5 and Jake Bates kicked for 15.4. Anuj spent $21 on Mike Gesicki, the biggest bid of the week, and started him at flex: two catches, eleven yards, 2.1. The Emmett Johnson file, entry four. Week 6: started, 5.4. Week 7: benched, 6.94. Week 8: benched, 26.06. Week 9: benched, a rushing touchdown, 10.56. Four weeks, four wrong calls, and Anuj has won three of them anyway. Maclane went from the worst lineup of the season to a perfect one. Lamar Jackson on IR, Aaron Rodgers on bye, Sam Darnold claimed for $0 on Wednesday and gone by Sunday. Michael Penix Jr., a Friday pickup, scored 14.48. Carson Schwesinger scored 18.5 at IDP. Demarcus Robinson, added at 12:38 on Sunday, started for 3.7, and it was still the best call available. The Vikings are gone; the Lions scored 11.04. 114.92, 100.0 percent, cleared the median by 0.88, the smallest margin of the week. 1-1. Jonathan Taylor ($62): 6.9 and a fumble.

Nathan ended the streak. Chris was 16-0, Nathan beat him by 11.72, and Nathan still missed the median by 3.14 and went 1-1, because 110.90 was the tenth score of the week. CeeDee Lamb caught ten balls for 195 yards, 30.5. Then the Kirk Cousins file, entry two. Week 8: benched for 28.18, Jayden Daniels started for 14.98. Week 9: benched for 15.64, Daniels started for 14.56. Wrong both weeks, by 13.20 and then 1.08. Efton Chism scored 13.4 on the bench. Nathan's best lineup goes 2-0. He is 12-6 with the best luck in the league. Chris: Josh Allen 13.86, Tyler Shough 19.7 on the bench. Tony Pollard on bye, zero. Jahmyr Gibbs ($73) 13.4 on a 22.71 projection, Kyren Williams 7.6. Chris picked up Eddy Pineiro, the Bears and Tyler Higbee inside three minutes on Wednesday morning. Pineiro kicked 8.5, the Bears never played for him, and Higbee caught one ball for 1.8 at tight end. The Chiefs, added at 11:42 on Saturday night, scored 14.0. 99.18, the lowest score in the league, 0-13 in all-play, 0-2. The best lineup scores 105.02: still the lowest score in the league. $95 of FAAB, untouched, now a monument.

Abhishek lost to the 1-11 team in Week 7 and the 3-11 team in Week 8. In Week 9 he drew Greg (IR) and won by 31.48. The 49ers, a $0 waiver claim, intercepted three passes and scored a touchdown: 21.24. Tank Dell, projected for 3.07, scored 19.54 at flex. Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked for 17.8. Chig Okonkwo, cut and then re-added on Saturday, scored 8.7 at the other flex. KaVontae Turpin, added Wednesday, scored zero on the bench. 133.16, 2-0. Greg (IR) started Josh Jacobs at flex. Yahoo projected Jacobs for 0.00. He ran for five yards: 0.5. Brock Purdy scored 26.28, Tyler Bass ($4) 13.6, and Terrance Ferguson ($3) went straight to injured reserve. Zay Flowers ($34) 4.8, Tucker Kraft 1.4. 101.68, 0-2. Greg's best lineup also goes 0-2. Six straight head-to-head losses, 40 moves, down four to eleventh.

178.78. The highest score of the season, 13-0 in all-play, and Barrett is now 17-1, 9-0 against the median, with a best-lineup record of 18-0. Jordan Love ($2) threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another: 36.18. Love has 192.02 points this season, for two dollars. Kenneth Walker ($43) scored three touchdowns, 35.3. Matthew Golden ($5) caught ten balls for 164 yards, 29.4. Ladd McConkey ($28) started and did not record a stat: 0.00. It did not matter at all. Will scored 140.42, the fourth-highest score of the week, 10-3 in all-play, and lost by 38.36. Joe Burrow scored 29.54 and Ja'Marr Chase 28.5. Then the bench: DeMario Douglas ($40) 13.7, Denzel Boston 12.8, Seth McGowan 10.7, while Malik Washington (3.1) and Josh Downs (3.9) started. 19.50 points of regret. The Jets defense scored 9.04 and is still starting. The median saved Will by 26.38. 6-12, the worst luck in the league at -2.15, and a best-lineup record of 11-7.

C.J. Stroud, a $1 auction quarterback, threw five touchdowns for 384 yards: 36.36, the best start of the week. James Cook scored 17.7, Travis Kelce 15.3 and the Jaguars 13.16. Cairo Santos, added Wednesday, kicked for 9.3 and Jordyn Brooks, added at 11:50 on Sunday, 8.0 at IDP. 99.1 percent, 143.96, 2-0. And the Keenan Allen Experience reaches its final form: benched, 5.6. The exact number he scored the one week Darrius started him. For once the bench was the right place. Jaxon Smith-Njigba ($63) scored 8.6 on a 21.08 projection. Tom lost by 44.28, scored 99.68, 1-12 in all-play, and went 0-2 for the third straight week. He spent $15 on Tuesday night: Kaelon Black ($12) scored 8.24 on the bench and the Texans ($3) 16.72 in the lineup. Romeo Doubs and Tyjae Spears were claimed for $0 and went straight to injured reserve. Derrick Henry ($45) ran for 57 yards and threw for minus three: 5.58. Aaron Jones 2.6 at flex. Brenton Strange 3.2. Six straight losses counting the median. The house is closed.

Andrew won by 48.40, the biggest margin of the week. Puka Nacua caught 14 balls, 31.0. Christian Watson scored 28.6 and Luther Burden 18.2. The Steelers were on bye, so on Sunday morning Andrew cut Alec Pierce and picked up the Giants: 14.5. Then the Kyle Pitts file. On the bench: 12.7, 20.5, 10.7. In the lineup: 1.6, and this week 3.8 at flex, with Chris Rodriguez scoring 10.2 on the bench. Justice Hill, added two weeks ago and benched for 5.5, scored 19.5 on the bench, while D'Andre Swift ($26) started and ran for 31 yards, 3.1, the worst start of the week against his projection. Devin Singletary ($8) started at the other back spot: 4.9. 22.80 points of regret and 2-0 anyway. Three straight wins. Greg (Miley) started Jared Goff for 6.30 with Bryce Young on the bench: three touchdowns, 21.34. Week 8: Goff 10.04 started, Young 12.36 benched. Wrong two weeks running, by 15.04 this time. Nick Bolton scored 10.5 on the bench while Travis Hunter scored 2.9 at IDP. Harrison Butker, a Thursday pickup, kicked for 5.0. Jaylen Waddle ($24) 2.7. 80.0 percent, the worst lineup of the week. 0-2, down two.
